description: Turn typed text into the location_slug every search takes: cities, neighborhoods, ZIPs, counties, states, schools and colleges.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
**What the user is typing**  -  a city, neighborhood, ZIP, county, state, school, college, base or
landmark name. Required; 2 to 100 characters.

- Partial words work (`aust` finds Austin), and a state narrows it (`austin tx`).
- A 5-digit ZIP returns that ZIP.
- Accents are ignored: `São Paulo` answers exactly as `Sao Paulo`.
- US place names only: a query with fewer than two letters or digits A - Z / 0 - 9 once accents are
  dropped (`Москва`, `日本`, `((`) is a 400.

Each suggestion carries the `location_slug` every location-scoped endpoint takes.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description:
**Only return these kinds of location.** Optional; every kind when omitted. Comma-separated:
`city,neighborhood`.

- `city`  -  a city or town.
- `neighborhood`  -  a neighborhood inside a city.
- `zip`  -  a ZIP code.
- `county`  -  a county.
- `state`  -  a US state.
- `school`  -  the area around a school.
- `school_district`  -  a school district.
- `college`  -  the area around a college or university.
- `military`  -  the area around a military base.
- `poi`  -  a named point of interest (a landmark, park or venue).

Several values are a union. Every suggestion reports its own `type`. Unknown values are a 400
naming the accepted values. For `county`, `school_district`, `school`, `college` and `military` a
bare name is enough: `query=harris&types=county` finds Harris County.

A state is suggested when the query is its full name or its two-letter code (`texas`, `tx`);
with `types=state`, states whose name starts with the query match too (`new` → New Hampshire,
New Jersey, New Mexico, New York  -  at most six states per query). The 50 states and DC are covered.

description: One location's name, centre, live rental count and GeoJSON boundary.

parameters.name: location_slug
parameters.description:
**The location, as a Rent.com location slug.** Required.

Take it from any `/locations` row. Slugs are readable paths:

- `texas/austin`  -  a city.
- `texas/austin/hyde-park-neighborhood`  -  a neighborhood.
- `zip-78701`  -  a ZIP code (a bare `78701` also works).
- `texas/counties/travis`  -  a county.
- `texas`  -  a whole state.
- `texas/university-of-texas--austin`  -  the area around a college (`~` stands for "&" and `_` for "/",
  e.g. `texas/texas-a~m-university`).

**Some locations are searched as a circle around their centre**  -  neighborhoods, colleges, many schools and
landmarks, and some cities  -  so results can include nearby listings outside the boundary. `/location-details`
reports the circle as `search_radius_miles`; where it is `null` (ZIP codes, counties, school districts, states
and many cities) the search follows the boundary.

Case and leading/trailing slashes are forgiven. A value that is not slug-shaped is a **400**; a
well-formed slug that names no location is a **404**.

parameters.name: include_boundary
parameters.description:
**Include the location's boundary polygon.** Optional; default `true`.

The boundary is a GeoJSON `Feature` ready to draw on a map. It is small for a neighborhood or ZIP
and can run to several megabytes for a big city or state, so send `false` when you only need the
name, centre, radius, box and `listing_count`  -  `boundary` is then `null`. A location with no outline
of its own (a college, most schools and landmarks, many small towns) returns `null` either way.

parameters.name: beds
parameters.description:

- `studio`  -  studio (0 bedrooms).
- `1`  -  one bedroom.
- `2`  -  two bedrooms.
- `3`  -  three bedrooms.

400 naming the accepted values.

parameters.name: amenities
parameters.description:
**Amenities the listing must have.** Optional. Comma-separated lower-case values:
`pool,washer_dryer_in_unit`.

**Several values are an intersection (AND)**  -  every listed amenity must be present, so each extra
value narrows (unlike `beds`, `baths` and `property_types`, which widen). Rare amenities often match
nothing within one city. An unknown value is a 400 naming it.

Aliases that match exactly the same listings:

- `balcony` = `patio`.
- `walk_in_closets` = `oversized_closets`.
- `pet_friendly` = `pet_policy=pet_friendly`.

Accepted values:

- **In the unit:** `air_conditioning`, `alarm` (alarm system), `ceiling_fan`, `dishwasher`, `extra_storage`, `fireplace`, `furnished_available` (furnished units offered), `garbage_disposal`, `gas_range`, `hardwood_floors`, `island_kitchens` (kitchen island), `loft_layout`, `microwave`, `new_renovated_interior`, `oversized_closets`, `recently_updated`, `refrigerator`, `remodeled`, `stainless_steel_appliances`, `vaulted_ceilings`, `walk_in_closets`, `washer_dryer_connections`, `washer_dryer_in_unit`.
- **Outdoor space and views:** `balcony`, `deck`, `patio`, `view`, `waterfront`.
- **Community facilities:** `basketball_courts`, `business_center`, `conference_room`, `elevator`, `fitness_center`, `green_community`, `hot_tub`, `laundry_facility`, `media_center`, `new_construction`, `pet_park`, `playground`, `pool`, `recreation_room`, `tennis_court`.
- **Parking and access:** `carport`, `controlled_access`, `disability_access`, `door_attendant`, `ev_charging`, `garage`, `gated_access`, `parking_available`.
- **Services:** `emergency_maintenance` (24-hour), `full_concierge_service`, `housekeeping_available`, `on_site_maintenance`, `se_habla_espanol` (Spanish-speaking staff), `virtual_tours` (virtual tour available).
- **Internet and bills:** `att_fiber` (AT&T Fiber available), `cable_ready`, `high_speed_internet_access`, `internet_included`, `utilities_included`, `wireless_internet_access`.
- **Lease and housing type:** `available_now` (move in now), `college` (student housing), `income_restricted` (affordable housing), `individual_leases` (by-the-bed leases), `military` (military housing), `pet_friendly`, `senior_living`, `short_term_available`, `smoke_free`.

Take it from any `/locations` row. Slugs are readable paths:

- `texas/austin`  -  a city.
- `texas/austin/hyde-park-neighborhood`  -  a neighborhood.

- `texas`  -  a whole state.

landmarks, and some cities  -  so results can include nearby listings outside the boundary. `/location-details`

and many cities) the search follows the boundary.

well-formed slug that names no location is a **404**.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
**How to order the results.** Optional; default `relevance`.

- `relevance`  -  Rent.com's own best-match order.
- `price_low_to_high`  -  cheapest rent first.
- `price_high_to_low`  -  most expensive rent first.
- `beds_low_to_high`  -  fewest bedrooms first (studios, then one-bedrooms, …).
- `sqft_low_to_high`  -  smallest interior first.
- `random`  -  a shuffled order, different on each call and each page (useful for sampling a market).

**Notes:**

- **Price orders** follow Rent.com's rent index, so a small share of rows sit slightly out of order
  against `price`. They leave out some listings that publish no rent (so `total` can be slightly lower)
  and list the other unpriced rows last, with `price` `null`.
- No newest or rating sort (filter with `updated_within_days` for recency), and no `distance`: it needs a named location and exists on `/search`, `/search-by-url` and `/agent-contacts`; rows here can be re-ranked by their own coordinates.
- **Paging:** for a near-complete crawl use a price order. `relevance`, `sqft_low_to_high` and
  `beds_low_to_high` break ties differently on each call, so paging through them can repeat or skip
  rows; `random` reshuffles every page. Only a single page (`total` ≤ `page_size`) is guaranteed
  complete.

  the single most telling word when in doubt.

values narrow sharply.

exclude_listing_ids.description:
**Listing ids to leave out.** Optional. Comma-separated, up to 200 ids:
`lc6705165,lv3221207700`.

Ids come from any row's `listing_id`  -  use it to skip rows you already hold. A malformed id is a 400;
an id that does not exist is simply not excluded.

exclude_city.description:
**A city to leave out.** Optional. One city `location_slug` from `/locations`, e.g. `texas/austin`.

  search route, `/search-nationwide` included.

  drops rows addressed to a neighbouring town that Rent.com files under the city, and keeps rows that
  Rent.com files under another town even when the search area covers them.

  names no location.

sort.description:
**How to order the results.** Optional; default `relevance`.

- `relevance`  -  Rent.com's own best-match order.
- `price_low_to_high`  -  cheapest rent first.
- `price_high_to_low`  -  most expensive rent first.
- `beds_low_to_high`  -  fewest bedrooms first (studios, then one-bedrooms, …).
- `sqft_low_to_high`  -  smallest interior first.
- `random`  -  a shuffled order, different on each call and each page (useful for sampling a market).

**Notes:**

  against `price`. They leave out some listings that publish no rent (so `total` can be slightly lower)
  and list the other unpriced rows last, with `price` `null`.

  rows; `random` reshuffles every page. Only a single page (`total` ≤ `page_size`) is guaranteed
  complete.

page.description:
**Which page of results to return.** Optional; default `1`, at most `10000`.

`has_more` (and `total_pages`, where returned) says when to stop; both count only the pages that can
actually be requested.

**A search can be paged through its first 100,000 results.** `page` × `page_size` may not exceed
100,000 (a deeper request is a 400); split the search with filters or a smaller area to reach further.

page_size.description:
**How many listings per page.** Optional; default `50`, maximum `500`.

Crawl at `500` to cover a market in the fewest calls; larger pages take a few
seconds longer to answer.

description: Search rentals inside a hand-drawn polygon.

parameters.name: polygon
parameters.description:
**The area to search, as a polygon.** Required.

Two formats are accepted:

- `lat,lng;lat,lng;…`  -  latitude first, points separated by `;`. At least 3 distinct points; the ring
  is closed for you. Example: `30.26,-97.75;30.26,-97.73;30.28,-97.73;30.28,-97.75` (a box over
  downtown Austin).
- A GeoJSON `Polygon` as a string (also a `Feature` wrapping one, or a single-part `MultiPolygon`)  - 
  GeoJSON order is **longitude first**. **Holes are honoured**: every ring after the first is cut out
  of the area, and must sit wholly inside the outline.

At most 200 points across all rings, clockwise or counter-clockwise; a point repeated
back-to-back is collapsed. A 400 answers:

- fewer than 3 distinct points in a ring, or points all on one straight line;
- an outline that crosses or doubles back on itself, or a hole outside the outline;
- a `MultiPolygon` with two or more parts (search each part separately);
- an unparseable value.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
**How to order the results.** Optional; default `relevance`.

- `relevance`  -  Rent.com's own best-match order.
- `price_low_to_high`  -  cheapest rent first.
- `price_high_to_low`  -  most expensive rent first.
- `beds_low_to_high`  -  fewest bedrooms first (studios, then one-bedrooms, …).
- `sqft_low_to_high`  -  smallest interior first.
- `random`  -  a shuffled order, different on each call and each page (useful for sampling a market).

**Notes:**

- **Price orders** follow Rent.com's rent index, so a small share of rows sit slightly out of order
  against `price`. They leave out some listings that publish no rent (so `total` can be slightly lower)
  and list the other unpriced rows last, with `price` `null`.
- No newest or rating sort (filter with `updated_within_days` for recency), and no `distance`: it needs a named location and exists on `/search`, `/search-by-url` and `/agent-contacts`; rows here can be re-ranked by their own coordinates.
- **Paging:** for a near-complete crawl use a price order. `relevance`, `sqft_low_to_high` and
  `beds_low_to_high` break ties differently on each call, so paging through them can repeat or skip
  rows; `random` reshuffles every page. Only a single page (`total` ≤ `page_size`) is guaranteed
  complete.

polygon.description:
**The area to search, as a polygon.** Required.

Two formats are accepted:

- `lat,lng;lat,lng;…`  -  latitude first, points separated by `;`. At least 3 distinct points; the ring
  is closed for you. Example: `30.26,-97.75;30.26,-97.73;30.28,-97.73;30.28,-97.75` (a box over
  downtown Austin).
- A GeoJSON `Polygon` as a string (also a `Feature` wrapping one, or a single-part `MultiPolygon`)  - 
  GeoJSON order is **longitude first**. **Holes are honoured**: every ring after the first is cut out
  of the area, and must sit wholly inside the outline.

At most 200 points across all rings, clockwise or counter-clockwise; a point repeated
back-to-back is collapsed. A 400 answers:

- fewer than 3 distinct points in a ring, or points all on one straight line;
- an outline that crosses or doubles back on itself, or a hole outside the outline;
- a `MultiPolygon` with two or more parts (search each part separately);
- an unparseable value.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
**How to order the results.** Optional; default `relevance`.

- `relevance`  -  Rent.com's own best-match order.
- `price_low_to_high`  -  cheapest rent first.
- `price_high_to_low`  -  most expensive rent first.
- `beds_low_to_high`  -  fewest bedrooms first (studios, then one-bedrooms, …).
- `sqft_low_to_high`  -  smallest interior first.
- `random`  -  a shuffled order, different on each call and each page (useful for sampling a market).

**Notes:**

- **Price orders** follow Rent.com's rent index, so a small share of rows sit slightly out of order
  against `price`. They leave out some listings that publish no rent (so `total` can be slightly lower)
  and list the other unpriced rows last, with `price` `null`.
- No newest or rating sort (filter with `updated_within_days` for recency), and no `distance`: it needs a named location and exists on `/search`, `/search-by-url` and `/agent-contacts`.
- **Paging:** for a near-complete crawl use `sqft_low_to_high` or a price order. `relevance` and
  `beds_low_to_high` break ties differently on each call, so paging through them can repeat or skip
  many rows; `random` reshuffles every page. Only a single page (`total` ≤ `page_size`) is guaranteed
  complete.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description:
**A Rent.com search or location page URL.** Required.

Examples: `https://www.rent.com/texas/austin-apartments`,
`https://www.rent.com/nevada/las-vegas-apartments/2-bedroom_2-bathroom`,
`https://www.rent.com/new-york/new-york-apartments/max-price-1300`,
`https://www.rent.com/texas/austin-apartments/hyde-park-neighborhood/pet-friendly`,
`https://www.rent.com/texas/austin/houses`, `https://www.rent.com/zip-78701-apartments`,
`https://www.rent.com/neighborhoods/texas/austin/hyde-park/`.

The path is `//-`, optionally followed by `/-neighborhood` and one
refinement segment whose words are joined by `_` (`2-bedroom_2-bathroom`). Refinement words:

- `studio`, `N-bedroom` (`4-bedroom` and up = 4+).
- `N-bathroom` (`3-bathroom` and up = 3+).
- `min-price-N`, `max-price-N` (whole dollars).
- `pet-friendly`, `dog-friendly`, `cat-friendly`, `no-pets`.
- `rent-deals-specials` (= `with_deals=true`), `cheap` (= `price_preference=cheap`).
- `furnished`, and any `/search` `amenities` value written with hyphens (`pool`, `utilities-included`).

filter behind it (`luxury`) is not applied at all and comes back in `unrecognised_segments`.

2,000 characters and 8 path segments. A listing page URL is a 400 pointing to `/listing-by-url`; a
URL from another site is a 400.

parameters.description:
**The location, as a Rent.com location slug.** Required.

Take it from any `/locations` row. Slugs are readable paths:

- `zip-78701`  -  a ZIP code (a bare `78701` also works).

reports the circle as `search_radius_miles`; where it is `null` (ZIP codes, counties, school districts, states
and many cities) the search follows the boundary.

Case and leading/trailing slashes are forgiven. A value that is not slug-shaped is a **400**; a
well-formed slug that names no location is a **404**.

**Amenities the listing must have.** Optional. Comma-separated lower-case values:
`pool,washer_dryer_in_unit`.

**Several values are an intersection (AND)**  -  every listed amenity must be present, so each extra
value narrows (unlike `beds`, `baths` and `property_types`, which widen). Rare amenities often match
nothing within one city. An unknown value is a 400 naming it.

Aliases that match exactly the same listings:

- `balcony` = `patio`.
- `walk_in_closets` = `oversized_closets`.
- `pet_friendly` = `pet_policy=pet_friendly`.

Accepted values:

- **In the unit:** `air_conditioning`, `alarm` (alarm system), `ceiling_fan`, `dishwasher`, `extra_storage`, `fireplace`, `furnished_available` (furnished units offered), `garbage_disposal`, `gas_range`, `hardwood_floors`, `island_kitchens` (kitchen island), `loft_layout`, `microwave`, `new_renovated_interior`, `oversized_closets`, `recently_updated`, `refrigerator`, `remodeled`, `stainless_steel_appliances`, `vaulted_ceilings`, `walk_in_closets`, `washer_dryer_connections`, `washer_dryer_in_unit`.
- **Outdoor space and views:** `balcony`, `deck`, `patio`, `view`, `waterfront`.
- **Community facilities:** `basketball_courts`, `business_center`, `conference_room`, `elevator`, `fitness_center`, `green_community`, `hot_tub`, `laundry_facility`, `media_center`, `new_construction`, `pet_park`, `playground`, `pool`, `recreation_room`, `tennis_court`.
- **Parking and access:** `carport`, `controlled_access`, `disability_access`, `door_attendant`, `ev_charging`, `garage`, `gated_access`, `parking_available`.
- **Services:** `emergency_maintenance` (24-hour), `full_concierge_service`, `housekeeping_available`, `on_site_maintenance`, `se_habla_espanol` (Spanish-speaking staff), `virtual_tours` (virtual tour available).
- **Internet and bills:** `att_fiber` (AT&T Fiber available), `cable_ready`, `high_speed_internet_access`, `internet_included`, `utilities_included`, `wireless_internet_access`.
- **Lease and housing type:** `available_now` (move in now), `college` (student housing), `income_restricted` (affordable housing), `individual_leases` (by-the-bed leases), `military` (military housing), `pet_friendly`, `senior_living`, `short_term_available`, `smoke_free`.

parameters.name: min_price
parameters.description:
**Lowest monthly rent to include, in whole US dollars.** Optional; no floor when omitted.

Send it alone for "at least", or with `max_price` for a window (`1500` and `2500`). A community
matches when any floor plan's rent range overlaps the window. `min_price` above `max_price` is a 400,
and so is a fraction (`999.5`).

Where listing rows are returned, each row's `filter_match` carries just the floor plans that matched.

parameters.name: move_in_date
parameters.description:
**Only listings with a unit available by this date.** Optional. Format `YYYY-MM-DD`, e.g. `2026-11-01`.

Keeps listings with a unit you could move into on or before the date. Availability dates are on

a single rental (`floor_plans[].available_date`). A malformed or impossible date (`2026-02-30`) is a 400.

Where listing rows are returned, each row's `filter_match` carries just the floor plans that matched.

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description:
**Free-text keyword to match.** Optional; up to 100 characters.

Matches words in the listing's own text  -  `luxury`, `rooftop`, `downtown`  -  and narrows sharply.
Accents are ignored: `café` matches what `cafe` does.

- **Several words match as an ordered phrase**: `luxury pool` does not match `pool … luxury`, so send
  the single most telling word when in doubt.
- There is no exclusion syntax: a leading `-` is ignored (`-luxury` matches what `luxury` does).

Blank is the same as omitting it. To find a community by name nationwide, use `/search-by-property-name`.

parameters.name: updated_within_days
parameters.description:
**Only listings updated within this many days.** Optional; `2` - `365`.

- `2`  -  the shortest window (`1` is a 400).
- `7`  -  refreshed this week.
- `30`  -  refreshed this month.

Judged against each row's `updated_at` (the last change to the listing on Rent.com), not listing age.
The window is counted in whole days, so it is approximate: `2` can include a row updated slightly
more than 48 hours ago.

parameters.name: exclude_city
parameters.description:
**A city to leave out.** Optional. One city `location_slug` from `/locations`, e.g. `texas/austin`.

- `location_slug=texas&exclude_city=texas/austin` searches Texas outside Austin; it works on every
  search route, `/search-nationwide` included.
- **The exclusion follows Rent.com's own city attribution, not the postal city on each row**: it also
  drops rows addressed to a neighbouring town that Rent.com files under the city, and keeps rows that
  Rent.com files under another town even when the search area covers them.
- One city per search. A ZIP, neighborhood, county or state slug is a 400, and so is a slug that
  names no location.

parameters.name: price_preference
parameters.description:
**Keep only the market's cheaper rentals.** Optional; a single value.

- `cheap`  -  listings renting at or under a per-market threshold that Rent.com sets and does not
  publish; the same result as a `max_price` at that threshold.

How it combines:

- It applies to cities, neighborhoods and ZIP codes. On a state, county or college area there is no
  threshold, and it only removes listings that publish no rent.
- **A `max_price` you send replaces the threshold**, even a higher one; a `min_price` combines with it
  into a window.
- On `/search` each row's `filter_match` carries the floor plans under the threshold, as with `max_price`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
**How to order the scanned listings.** Optional; default `price_high_to_low`, because agent-listed
rentals cluster at the expensive end of a market, so it yields the most contacts per scanned page.

- `relevance`  -  Rent.com's own best-match order.
- `price_low_to_high`  -  cheapest rent first.
- `price_high_to_low`  -  most expensive rent first.
- `beds_low_to_high`  -  fewest bedrooms first (studios, then one-bedrooms, …).
- `sqft_low_to_high`  -  smallest interior first.
- `random`  -  a shuffled order, different on each call and each page (useful for sampling a market).
- `distance`  -  nearest the location's centre first (the centre `/location-details` reports). Rent.com
  ranks a group of lower-priority listings after the rest, again nearest first; every row carries
  `distance_miles` for a strict local re-sort.

**Notes:**

- **Price orders** follow Rent.com's rent index, so a small share of rows sit slightly out of order
  against `price`. They leave out some listings that publish no rent (so `total` can be slightly lower)
  and list the other unpriced rows last, with `price` `null`.
- No newest or rating sort: filter with `updated_within_days` for recency.
- **Paging:** for a complete, duplicate-free crawl use `price_low_to_high`, `price_high_to_low` or
  `sqft_low_to_high`; `distance` misses at most a few rows. `relevance` and `beds_low_to_high` break
  ties differently on each call, so paging through them can repeat or skip rows; `random` reshuffles
  every page.

location_slug.description:
**The location, as a Rent.com location slug.** Required.

Take it from any `/locations` row. Slugs are readable paths:

- `texas/austin`  -  a city.
- `texas/austin/hyde-park-neighborhood`  -  a neighborhood.
- `zip-78701`  -  a ZIP code (a bare `78701` also works).
- `texas/counties/travis`  -  a county.
- `texas`  -  a whole state.
- `texas/university-of-texas--austin`  -  the area around a college (`~` stands for "&" and `_` for "/",
  e.g. `texas/texas-a~m-university`).

**Some locations are searched as a circle around their centre**  -  neighborhoods, colleges, many schools and
landmarks, and some cities  -  so results can include nearby listings outside the boundary. `/location-details`
reports the circle as `search_radius_miles`; where it is `null` (ZIP codes, counties, school districts, states
and many cities) the search follows the boundary.

Case and leading/trailing slashes are forgiven. A value that is not slug-shaped is a **400**; a
well-formed slug that names no location is a **404**.

beds.description:
**Bedroom counts to include.** Optional. Comma-separated for several: `1,2`.

- `studio`  -  studio (0 bedrooms).
- `1`  -  one bedroom.
- `2`  -  two bedrooms.
- `3`  -  three bedrooms.
- `4_plus`  -  four or more bedrooms.

**Several values are a union (OR)**: `1,2` returns listings offering a one-bedroom **or** a
two-bedroom. A community matches when any of its floor plans has the count. Unknown values are a
400 naming the accepted values.

Where listing rows are returned, each row's `filter_match` carries just the floor plans that matched.

- `1`  -  one bathroom.
- `2`  -  two bathrooms.
- `3_plus`  -  three or more bathrooms.

**Several values are a union (OR)**, the same as `beds`. A community matches when any of its floor
plans has the count. Unknown values are a 400 naming the accepted values.

Where listing rows are returned, each row's `filter_match` carries just the floor plans that matched.

property_types.description:
**Kinds of property to include.** Optional. Comma-separated for several: `houses,townhouses`.

- `apartments`  -  apartment communities and units.
- `houses`  -  single-family houses; **also returns duplex-type rows** (send `duplexes` alone for
  duplexes only).
- `townhouses`  -  townhouses and townhomes.
- `duplexes`  -  duplexes.
- `condos`  -  condominiums.
- `triplexes`  -  triplexes.

**Several values are a union (OR).** The singular `property_type` a row reports (`house`, `condo`,
`townhome`, `duplex`, `triplex`, `apartment`) is accepted as an alias, so a row's type can be fed
straight back. Unknown values are a 400 naming the accepted values.

pet_policy.description:
**Pet policy the listing must allow.** Optional; a single value.

- `cats_ok`  -  cats allowed.
- `dogs_ok`  -  dogs allowed.
- `pet_friendly`  -  cats **or** dogs allowed (a listing that takes only one still matches).
- `no_pets`  -  listings that do not accept pets.

There is no "cats and dogs" value: filter with `cats_ok` and check the `pet_policies` array on
`/listing-details`, which carries each policy with its deposit, fee, pet rent and weight limit.

**Only listings updated within this many days.** Optional; `2` - `365`.

- `30`  -  refreshed this month.

- `transit`  -  stations, bus stops and tram stops.
